Build a Chrome Extension MVP for Rankora — a resume ranking SaaS at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora`. Read `CLAUDE.md` first for context.

## IMPORTANT — Concurrency
Two other agents are working on the codebase in parallel. DO NOT modify any existing files in `src/`, `supabase/functions/`, or `supabase/migrations/`. Only create new files in a NEW `chrome-extension/` directory at the repo root.

If you need backend API support, create a NEW edge function in `supabase/functions/extension-capture/` but do NOT touch any existing edge functions.

## The Feature
A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that:
1. User installs the extension and logs in using their Rankora API key (from existing `/integrations` page → API tab)
2. While browsing LinkedIn profiles or GitHub profiles, user clicks the extension icon
3. Extension reads the page, extracts candidate info (name, title, company, location, profile URL)
4. Sends data to Rankora via the existing public REST API (`/functions/v1/public-api`)
5. Candidate is added to the user's talent pool
6. Extension shows success toast

## Build Plan

### 1. Directory structure
```
chrome-extension/
├── manifest.json
├── popup.html
├── popup.css
├── popup.js
├── content-script.js
├── background.js
├── icons/
│   ├── icon-16.png
│   ├── icon-48.png
│   └── icon-128.png
└── README.md
```

### 2. `manifest.json` (Manifest V3)
```json
{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "Rankora — Candidate Capture",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Capture candidate profiles from LinkedIn and GitHub to your Rankora talent pool with one click.",
  "permissions": ["activeTab", "storage", "scripting"],
  "host_permissions": [
    "https://www.linkedin.com/*",
    "https://github.com/*",
    "https://*.rankora.co/*",
    "https://*.supabase.co/*"
  ],
  "action": {
    "default_popup": "popup.html",
    "default_icon": {
      "16": "icons/icon-16.png",
      "48": "icons/icon-48.png",
      "128": "icons/icon-128.png"
    }
  },
  "background": {
    "service_worker": "background.js"
  },
  "content_scripts": [
    {
      "matches": [
        "https://www.linkedin.com/in/*",
        "https://github.com/*"
      ],
      "js": ["content-script.js"],
      "run_at": "document_idle"
    }
  ],
  "icons": {
    "16": "icons/icon-16.png",
    "48": "icons/icon-48.png",
    "128": "icons/icon-128.png"
  }
}
```

### 3. `popup.html`
- Clean, branded UI matching Rankora design
- Shows current state:
  - NOT LOGGED IN: input for API key + "Save API Key" button + link to Rankora dashboard
  - LOGGED IN: shows "Capture This Profile" button + detected candidate preview (name, title, company) + "Logout" link
- Shows status messages (loading, success, error)

### 4. `popup.css`
- Tailwind-like utility styling inline (no build step for extension)
- Match Rankora brand: primary blue, clean sans-serif, rounded corners
- Max width 360px
- Light mode only for MVP

### 5. `popup.js`
- On load: check chrome.storage.local for API key
- If no key: show login form
- If key exists:
  - Query active tab
  - Send message to content script: `{ action: 'extractProfile' }`
  - Content script returns: `{ name, title, company, location, profile_url, bio }`
  - Show preview
  - "Capture" button: POST to `${API_BASE}/functions/v1/public-api/candidates` with Bearer token
  - On success: show confirmation + "Go to Rankora" link
  - On error: show error message

### 6. `content-script.js`
- Listens for messages from popup
- On `extractProfile`:
  - If URL matches linkedin.com/in/:
    - Extract: `.text-heading-xlarge` for name, `.text-body-medium` for title, `.pv-text-details__right-panel` for company, `.text-body-small:not(.inline)` for location
    - profile_url = window.location.href
    - Return extracted data
  - If URL matches github.com/:username:
    - Extract: `h1.vcard-names .p-name` for name, `.p-nickname` for username, `.vcard-details .p-label` for location, `.p-note .user-profile-bio` for bio
    - Return extracted data
- Note: selectors may vary — use multiple fallbacks and `document.querySelector` safely

### 7. `background.js`
- Service worker
- Handle any long-running tasks (e.g., API retries)
- Keep minimal for MVP

### 8. NEW Edge Function: `supabase/functions/extension-capture/index.ts`
Since the existing public-api may not support talent pool capture, create a dedicated one:
- Accepts POST with Bearer token (API key from existing api_keys table)
- Body: `{ name, email?, phone?, profile_url, source: 'linkedin'|'github'|'other', title?, company?, location?, bio? }`
- Validates API key by querying api_keys table
- Creates a new row in the resumes table with minimal data (parsed_json contains the profile info)
- Optionally adds to talent_pool table if user has one
- Returns `{ success: true, candidate_id }`
- CORS: allow all origins (`*`) since it's called from chrome-extension://

### 9. `README.md`
- Installation instructions: "Load unpacked" from chrome://extensions
- How to get API key from Rankora dashboard
- Supported sites: LinkedIn, GitHub
- Known limitations

### 10. Icons (placeholder)
- Since I can't generate images, create placeholder SVG icons and include instructions to replace with branded icons:
  - `icons/icon-16.svg`, `icons/icon-48.svg`, `icons/icon-128.svg`  
  - Simple "R" logo in primary color (#6366f1)
  - Note in README that these need to be converted to PNG for production

## Critical Requirements
- Pure vanilla JS (no build step, no frameworks) — keep it simple for Chrome extension
- No external dependencies in the extension (no npm)
- The extension must work immediately after "Load unpacked"
- Error handling for:
  - No API key
  - Invalid API key (401)
  - Page doesn't match supported sites
  - Missing candidate data
  - Network failure
- All styling inline or in popup.css
- Save API key securely in chrome.storage.local
- Allow updating the API base URL (default: https://zkzontawprihrzpayeam.supabase.co)

## Reference Patterns
- Existing edge function auth: look at `supabase/functions/public-api/index.ts` for the API key validation pattern
- Do NOT modify public-api — create extension-capture as a separate function

Build this feature end to end. Commit and push when done with a clear commit message. Report what you built when finished.

139	## Architecture Rules
140	
141	1. **Auth-first:** All data access uses Supabase RLS policies. Never bypass auth.
142	2. **shadcn-ui only:** Use components from `src/components/ui/`. No other UI libraries.
143	3. **Path aliases:** Always import with `@/` prefix (maps to `src/`).
144	4. **React Query:** All server state via React Query hooks. No raw `useEffect` for data fetching.
145	5. **Single Supabase client:** Import from `@/integrations/supabase/client.ts`. Never create new clients.
146	6. **Edge Functions:** Business logic in Supabase Edge Functions (Deno). Frontend calls via `supabase.functions.invoke()`.
147	7. **Credits system:** All ranking operations deduct credits via `deduct_credits()` DB function.
148	8. **Admin audit:** Log all admin mutations via `logAuditAction()` from `@/lib/auditLog.ts`.
149	9. **No hardcoded secrets:** All keys via environment variables (VITE_ prefix for frontend).
150	10. **Auto-generated types:** `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` is auto-generated. Do not manually edit.
151	11. **Sonner toasts:** Use `toast.success()`, `toast.error()` from sonner. No other notification system.
152	12. **Error handling:** Try-catch with toast for user-facing errors. Validation errors as arrays displayed inline.
153	13. **Real-time subscriptions:** Feature flags and SEO settings use Supabase real-time subscriptions + React Query invalidation.
154	
155	## Key Data Flows
156	
157	### Resume Ranking Pipeline
158	```
159	User enters JD + uploads files
160	→ validateFields() checks input
161	→ Create job record (status: pending)
162	→ analyzeJd() → analyze-jd edge function → stores jd_analysis_json
163	→ uploadFilesFromSnapshot() → Supabase Storage + resume records
164	→ rank-resumes edge function (GPT-4o scoring, skill matching)

def create_simple_png(size, color_rgb):

    size: (width, height)
    color_rgb: (r, g, b) tuple
    """
    width, height = size
    r, g, b = color_rgb

    # PNG signature
    signature = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'

    # IHDR chunk
    ihdr_data = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    ihdr_crc = zlib.crc32(b'IHDR' + ihdr_data) & 0xffffffff
    ihdr = struct.pack('>I', 13) + b'IHDR' + ihdr_data + struct.pack('>I', ihdr_crc)

    # IDAT chunk — raw image data
    raw_rows = []
    for _ in range(height):
        row = b'\x00'  # filter type none
        for _ in range(width):
            row += bytes([r, g, b])
        raw_rows.append(row)
    raw_data = b''.join(raw_rows)

# Rankora — Candidate Capture Chrome Extension

Capture candidate profiles from LinkedIn and GitHub into your Rankora talent pool with one click.

## Installation (Development / Local)

1. Open Chrome and navigate to `chrome://extensions`
2. Enable **Developer mode** (toggle in top-right corner)
3. Click **Load unpacked**
4. Select the `chrome-extension/` folder from this repository
5. The Rankora icon will appear in your Chrome toolbar

> For production distribution, package as a `.crx` or submit to the Chrome Web Store.

## Setup

1. Log in to your Rankora dashboard at [app.rankora.co](https://app.rankora.co)
2. Go to **Settings → Integrations → API Keys**
3. Generate a new API key (starts with `rk_live_`)
4. Click the Rankora extension icon in Chrome
5. Paste your API key and click **Connect**

## Usage

1. Navigate to a LinkedIn profile (`linkedin.com/in/...`) or GitHub profile (`github.com/username`)
2. Click the Rankora extension icon in the toolbar
3. The extension reads the page and shows a candidate preview (name, title, company, location)
4. Click **Capture to Talent Pool**
5. The candidate is added to your Rankora talent pool instantly

## Supported Sites

| Site | URL Pattern | Data Extracted |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| LinkedIn | `linkedin.com/in/:username` | Name, headline/title, company, location, about |
| GitHub | `github.com/:username` | Name, username, bio, company, location |

## Error States

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| "Navigate to a profile" | Not on LinkedIn/GitHub profile page | Open a profile URL |
| "Could not extract candidate info" | Page layout changed or loaded slowly | Refresh the page and try again |
| "API key is invalid or revoked" | Key expired or revoked | Generate a new key in Rankora settings |
| "Candidate already in talent pool" | Duplicate capture | Profile already saved |
| "Network error" | No internet connection | Check your connection |

## Icons

The `icons/` directory contains:
- `icon-16.svg`, `icon-48.svg`, `icon-128.svg` — SVG sources (indigo "R" logo)
- `icon-16.png`, `icon-48.png`, `icon-128.png` — PNG versions (auto-generated, solid indigo)

**For production:** Replace the PNG files with proper branded icons using a design tool or image processing library. The SVG sources are the reference.

## Architecture

```
popup.html / popup.js    — Extension UI (login, preview, capture)
content-script.js        — Injected into tab; extracts profile data from DOM
background.js            — Service worker; handles tab state, badge
icons/                   — Extension icons (16, 48, 128px)
```

**Backend:** `supabase/functions/extension-capture/index.ts`
- Validates API key (same SHA-256 hash pattern as `public-api`)
- Creates a sentinel "talent pool" job per user (once)
- Inserts a `resumes` row with `parsed_json` containing profile metadata
- Returns `{ success, candidate_id, candidate_name }`

## Security

- API key stored in `chrome.storage.local` (not accessible to web pages)
- Key validated server-side by SHA-256 hash — never stored in plaintext
- CORS is open (`*`) — required for `chrome-extension://` origin calls
- All inputs sanitized and length-capped server-side
- Duplicate detection prevents double-capture of the same profile URL

## Known Limitations (MVP)

- LinkedIn DOM selectors may break when LinkedIn updates their markup — update selectors in `content-script.js`
- GitHub organization pages are not supported (user profiles only)
- No bulk capture — one profile at a time
- Talent pool resumes are stored without a real file (profile URL used as file_path)
- No credit deduction for captured profiles (talent pool is free)

## Development

No build step required. The extension uses vanilla JavaScript with no dependencies.

To modify:
1. Edit files directly
2. Go to `chrome://extensions` → click the refresh icon on the Rankora extension
3. Test on a LinkedIn or GitHub profile page

## Deploying the Edge Function

```bash
supabase functions deploy extension-capture
```

The function reads:
- `SUPABASE_URL` — auto-injected by Supabase

All files are committed and pushed. Here is a complete summary of what was built:

---

## What was built

### Chrome Extension (`chrome-extension/`)

**14 files, zero dependencies, no build step required.**

`manifest.json` — Manifest V3 with `activeTab`, `storage`, and `scripting` permissions. Content scripts target `linkedin.com/in/*` and `github.com/*`. Service worker is `background.js`.

`popup.html` + `popup.css` — Branded 360px popup with three logical views:
- Login view: API key input + validation + link to Rankora dashboard
- Main view: loading state → candidate preview card (name, title, company badge, location badge) → capture button
- Success view: confirmation with "View in Rankora" and "Capture another" actions

`popup.js` — Full state machine. Reads API key from `chrome.storage.local`, sends `extractProfile` message to content script via `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`, falls back to `chrome.scripting.executeScript` if content script not yet injected. Validates API key format client-side (`rk_live_` prefix), verifies against the edge function's `/verify` route before saving. POST to `extension-capture` with Bearer token. Handles 401, 409 (duplicate), and network failures distinctly.

`content-script.js` — LinkedIn extractor uses 5+ selector fallbacks per field (name, headline/title, company, location, bio) because LinkedIn's DOM changes frequently. GitHub extractor reads `p-name`, `p-label`, `p-note`, `vcard-detail` itemprop fields. Falls back to `og:title` / `document.title` if no name found from DOM. Strips query params from profile URL.

`background.js` — MV3 service worker. Sets tab badge when user is on a supported page. Handles `ping` message for future use.

`icons/` — SVG sources (indigo #6366f1 "R" logo, 16/48/128px) plus generated solid-color PNG files required by Chrome.

### Edge Function (`supabase/functions/extension-capture/index.ts`)

New dedicated function — existing `public-api` was not touched.

- Authenticates via the exact same SHA-256 `key_hash` lookup pattern used by `public-api`
- `POST /extension-capture/verify` — key-only auth check (used by popup login flow to validate key before saving)
- `POST /extension-capture` — full capture flow:
  1. Validates name and profile_url required; profile_url must include `linkedin.com` or `github.com`
  2. Deduplicates by `parsed_json->>'profile_url'` — returns 409 if already captured for this user's jobs
  3. Creates a single sentinel job per user (`__rankora_talent_pool__`) on first capture
  4. Inserts a `resumes` row with `status: done`, `parsed_json` containing all profile metadata, `parsed_text` for future search
  5. Returns `{ success, candidate_id, candidate_name }`
- CORS `*` — required for `chrome-extension://` origin
- Fires `last_used_at` update on the API key (fire-and-forget, identical to `public-api`)

1. Go to `chrome://extensions`, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, select `chrome-extension/`
2. Deploy the edge function: `supabase functions deploy extension-capture`
3. Get an API key from Rankora Settings → Integrations → API Keys
4. Open LinkedIn or GitHub profile, click the extension icon, connect with your key, capture
